For those requiring a detailed history on the acrimony at the heart of this storied rivalry, look no further than Sam Wallace’s excellent essay, which explains why this tie will always be more than just a football match.

Here’s a snippet of Sam on the fixture’s most infamous chapter: the 1986 World Cup quarter-final, which took place four years after the Falklands War.

“You can’t grasp what it all means to the people back home, but something tells you it is the greatest experience you will have as a player.” Gary Lineker, with a hat-trick against Poland and two more goals in the last-16 win over Paraguay, had assessed the mood correctly before England’s match against Argentina at the Estadio Azteca. But even he could not have guessed what was to come.

The war between Britain and Argentina, just four years earlier, hung heavily over the game. “I am a football manager, not a politician,” Bobby Robson, the England manager, said: “Don’t ask me that sort of question.”

Midfielder Glenn Hoddle warned that Maradona had learned from his experiences at the 1982 World Cup and “really come on strong”. He pondered whether England should man-mark Maradona and suggested left-back Kenny Sansom. “I don’t think we should change the way we play because of him,” Hoddle said. “You would have to re-shape the whole side.”

The Argentine players gave each of the England team a present before the game. Maradona punched the ball into the England goal in the 51st minute. His brilliant second was four minutes later. Lineker scored his sixth of the tournament and England lost 2-1.

In just over 10 hours time we will know the identity of Spain’s World Cup final opponents after the European champions dispatched 2018 winners and pre-tournament favourites France on Tuesday evening.

Immortality beckons for England, who are braced for their biggest match in a generation with familiar foes Argentina standing between them and a first World Cup final since 1966.

This is a fixture steeped in history. The two nations are meeting at a World Cup for the sixth time, renewing a bitter rivalry that has produced some of the tournament’s most memorable moments and enduring controversies.

Thomas Tuchel’s side have reached the last four without being entirely convincing. They needed extra time to beat Norway in the quarter-finals after surviving for over half an hour with 10 men against co-hosts Mexico in the previous round.

England’s fortunes have been intrinsically linked to the performances of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham, who have scored six goals apiece to keep Tuchel’s side alive at this tournament.

Argentina’s route to the latter stages has been just as arduous. The defending champions needed extra time to overcome both Cape Verde and Switzerland, while they came from 2-0 down with 11 minutes remaining to beat Egypt and avoid one of the biggest shocks in World Cup history.

The holders remain on course to become only the third side after Italy (1934, 1938) and Brazil (1958, 1962) to retain their crown and in the process give Lionel Messi the fairy-tale end to a remarkable international career.

The 39-year-old has scored eight goals in the tournament and remains central to everything to Argentina’s fortunes. Remarkably, despite a career spanning more than two decades, tonight’s semi-final meeting will be Messi’s first ever international appearance against England.

Tuchel has spoken openly about the scale of the challenge facing his players. Stopping Messi has become one of football’s great unsolved problems, but the 52-year-old German insists his team must focus on imposing their own game plan rather than being consumed with the

Rarely has so much been at stake for both nations. For England, it is another chance to move one step closer to ending a wait that has now stretched almost 60 years. For Argentina, it is an opportunity to go level with Italy and Germany for the second-most World Cup titles (four). Either way, one of football’s most storied rivalries is about to add another chapter.

#2237. Kieran McKenna on West Ham’s three-man managerial shortlist as Nuno doubts grow

West Ham slipped to 8th in the Championship after defeat against West Brom on Saturday. WHUFC are currently in the play-off positions, but back-to-back losses to fellow promotion hopefuls have brought concerns.

Now, reporter Alan Nixon states that the Hammers have a three-man shortlist of potential targets if they decide to part ways with the under-fire Nuno Espirito Santo. Nixon says that Kieran McKenna, Rob Edwards and Scott Parker are all on the radar at the London Stadium.

All of the names mentioned are currently available, but it remains to be seen if the interest develops into anything concrete.

West Ham have some favourable fixtures coming up, with Cardiff City, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Portsmouth all to play before the end of November. This run could be crucial for Nuno as pressure on his position grows.

Unlike Championship rivals Burnley, who have recently appointed Fabio Celestini, it appears West Ham are looking for experience in the division as they weigh up potential Nuno replacements.

It may be hard to persuade McKenna to return to the second tier, however, Parker and Edwards may be tempted by the opportunity.

Parker has gained promotion from the Championship with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. He operated with possession-based football and defensive organisation within his ranks. However, his time at each club ended on a sour note in the Premier League with relegation campaigns.

Edwards has also gained promotion from the division with Luton Town, whilst showing positive signs at the likes of Middlesbrough. He deploys his sides with a compact, high-energy system, putting an emphasis on pressing and attacking width.

McKenna meanwhile has only managed Ipswich Town, taking them from League One to the Premier League. He left the club earlier this year, but the Tractor Boys would still be owed a sizeable compensation fee.

Although Parker has multiple promotions on his CV, a move for the Englishman may be a risk. He might take West Ham out of the Championship, but his spells at other clubs has indicated that he may not be able to keep them in the Premier League if they return.

McKenna would be a very exciting appointment for West Ham, however it would be a surprise to see him drop to the Championship again. He is the most attractive target of the three, but the most unlikely.

Edwards, may be a more feasible appointment though. He’s proven his promotion pedigree in the Championship and takes pride two things WHUFC are currently lacking: defensive organisation and battling spirit.

Time will tell if Nuno can turn the tide, but the Hammers are seemingly prepared if they do opt for change.

#2236. Middlesbrough should be optimistic about 21-year-old’s future amid bright loan stint for struggling League One side

Middlesbrough have built a squad that is readily challenging for promotion to the Premier League. Boro currently sit top of the Championship and have responded well to their play-off final defeat last season.

As a result of their big spending in the summer, several loans were sanctioned for players whose game time would be questionable. Out of the three departing for the campaign, Finley Munroe is the player for Kim Hellberg to monitor closely.

Middlesbrough signed the 21-year-old from Aston Villa in January 2026 after impressing on loan at Swindon Town. Now with his move to Blackpool almost three months in, Boro’s prospect is finding some success at Bloomfield Road.

Munroe has made a step-up this season despite being sent out on loan by Middlesbrough. Last campaign, the 21-year-old was playing in League Two and now he is playing in the third tier.

Despite just five starts in the league for Blackpool so far, the left-back has made a good account of himself. The youngster has made eight successful dribbles and won 57 duels. He has just featured at left-back in League One action, and his tenacity is evident with 31 tackles made.

He has been on the bench for the Tangerines’ last three outings, but he has done well to compete with Ilmari Niskanen for a starting XI spot. Munroe’s best display for his loan club came in a 2-2 draw with Bromley back in September.

The 21-year-old grabbed an assist and won 86% of his ground duels. While the Middlesbrough prospect may not have featured as much as they would’ve liked, there has certainly been many positives to take from his stint away from the Riverside.

Middlesbrough currently have two senior left-backs at the club with Neto Borges and Alex Bangura. The former has been Hellberg’s go-to option as the Brazilian has appeared in all 13 league games this season.

His performances have been quality too, with 131 line-breaking passes made and 16 chances created. Defensively, the 30-year-old has been astute too. He has made 50 recoveries and blocked seven shots.

Munroe’s first-team chances are slimmer next season if Borges remains and certainly so if they achieve promotion to the Premier League. That being said, the Brazilian could be a perfect role model for the 21-year-old to learn from, and a position off the bench could be necessary for the youngster.

With the youngster’s ability to play further forward on the left wing too, it does improve his chances of breaking into the first team. However, for his development’s sake, Boro must identify his natural position and work on strengthening him in that specific area.

#2235. Josh Windass reacts as Sheffield Wednesday set to confirm Clint Hill decision

There has been plenty of movement and activity at Sheffield Wednesday in recent weeks, with David Storch making his biggest call yet by parting ways with Henrik Pedersen following some mixed form in the opening months of the 2026/27 campaign.

Storch and co opted to retain Pedersen's position in the dugout in the aftermath of Wednesday's 0-point relegation from the Championship last season, which, of course, was blitzed by numerous points deductions upon an already-depleted and threadbare squad, as the club's key decision-makers believed that the Dane was the right man to spearhead a fresh promotion charge at Hillsborough.

A new-look squad featuring 18 new signings served to bolster those ambitions, though Pedersen would ultimately fail to deliver on the Owls' goals by winning five of his 11 matches of the current League One campaign, leaving his side outside the play-offs in eighth place following consecutive 2-0 defeats at Notts County and Doncaster Rovers before being dismissed in a move that brought his 15-month stay in the Steel City to an abrupt end.

Wednesday would act quickly, and, this time, met expectations with the appointment of former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor, who had previously been touted as a potential successor to Pedersen if he were to depart.

Challinor, having worked closely under Owls sporting director Simon Wilson during their fruitful time together at Edgeley Park, will be accompanied by another ex-Stockport figure in the form of Clint Hill - and an interesting reaction to the development has come from none other than Josh Windass.

Hill, who graced both the Championship and the Premier League during a lengthy playing career which took in notable spells with Stoke City, Crystal Palace and QPR before hanging up the boots and sinking his teeth into coaching, will be joining former teammate Challinor at Wednesday, as per a fresh report from The Star.

The 48-year-old would begin his career alongside Challinor at Tranmere Rovers, and they eventually reunited years later when the soon-to-be-unveiled Wednesday boss was managing Hartlepool United.

Challinor took Hill to Stockport in 2021 as his assistant manager, and the pair would enjoy four successful years in Greater Manchester prior to departing together after County's 4-1 play-off final defeat against Bolton Wanderers at the end of the previous campaign.

Hill's playing days were well-travelled, though, and, having briefly crossed paths with Windass at Rangers in the 2017/18 season, the current Wrexham forward has now sent a message to his ex-Ibrox teammate as he prepares to get stuck into proceedings in the blue-and-white quarters of the Steel City.

Speaking via a story post on his Instagram account, Windass only required six words to warmly wish Hill the very best of luck at a club he, of course, knows all-too-well.

Windass wrote: "Good luck at hillsborough big man 🔥🦉❤️ ."

FLW's Sheffield Wednesday fan pundit has discussed the prospect of Barry Bannan becoming the manager one day

The caption was accompanied by an image of the pair celebrating together at Rangers, where the attacker scored 19 goals in a mixed two-year spell before moving on to Wigan Athletic and then Wednesday.

Windass, having found the back of the net on no fewer than 50 occasions from 173 appearances across five seasons for Wednesday, has naturally kept a close eye on his former side since leaving to join Wrexham in July of last year.

The nature of Windass' departure, which came amid heightened turmoil at the hands of Dejphon Chansiri whereby multiple wage payments to both playing and non-playing staff were missed, left Owls fans divided and, as far as some were concerned, blighted the 32-year-old's legacy.

That hasn't prevented the Wrexham starlet from remaining very much in the loop with Wednesday's fortunes, however, and he will only have even greater incentive to monitor his old employers as Hill's appointment nears.

Barnsley 0-1 Sheffield Wednesday (after extra time), Wembley, 29 May 2023. Type the surnames of Darren Moore's starting XI. Every player you get drops onto the pitch.

You have 90 seconds. Surnames are enough.

Josh Windass headed in Lee Gregory's cross in the 123rd minute to send the Owls up.

It's an interesting connection, and Windass knows exactly what Hill is all about despite only spending one campaign with the seasoned ex-defender at the tail-end of his career.

Wednesday supporters are eagerly anticipating Challinor's appointment in light of such a strong body of work at Stockport, and they will only be pleased that he's going to be joined across the Pennines by his most trusted lieutenant.

With Hill operating as second-in-command, Challinor took Stockport from ninth in the National League to two successive League One play-off finishes in under five years.

He became one of the EFL's most highly-rated managers as a result, and his proven expertise at this level holds serious weight despite ultimately falling short of taking Stockport over the finish line.

But Hill's own involvement in that success, following the sort of esteemed playing career which always demands respect and authority, means that Wednesday fans should view his impending reunion with Challinor as a significant boost.

Their successful working relationship with the aforementioned Wilson means it should be a relatively seamless transition away from the field, too, and, if they can conjure up anything resemblant of a repeat on their Stockport magic, then Wednesdayites will be in for a treat.

#2234. Ex-Ipswich Town, Nottingham Forest & Middlesbrough star confirms major life decision

Mustapha Carayol, a winger who made over 250 EFL appearances across all three divisions, has announced his retirement.

The 38-year-old cut his teeth in the lower leagues, being a personal favourite of ex-Manchester United midfielder Paul Ince in his first coaching roles, who brought him to Swindon Town, Macclesfield Town and then MK Dons, where he signed his first professional contract in 2007.

In the 19 years since, Carayol bounced around numerous EFL sides, namely Bristol Rovers, Middlesbrough, Nottingham Forest, Ipswich Town and Burton Albion, but he also had loan spells with the likes of Brighton and Hove Albion, Huddersfield Town and Leeds United.

Having returned to the non-league circuit with Wealdstone and then Peterborough Sports last season, the seven-time Gambian international has called time on his professional career.

Taking to social media, Carayol penned a retirement message, thanking all the clubs he'd played for in both England and during short stints in Turkey and Cyprus in the late 2010s, the latter seeing him play in the Europa League with Apollon Limassol.

"From where it all began at the Damiola Taylor centre in Peckham to a 20-year career in football, what a journey it's been," he wrote. "After two decades, this chapter of my life has finally come to an end. I've learned so much along the way and will forever be grateful for everything football has given me.

"I got to live my dream of playing for my country. I wish I'd done it earlier, but standing out there on the pitch, my family in the stands and Gambians cheering my name, is something dreams are made of.

"To every teammate and staff member I've shared a dressing room, a training pitch or a bus journey with, you've all been a part of this story. To my family, none of this happens without you. Your love and support carried me every step of the way.

"And to my son, getting to play with you watching was always my dream. I'm so grateful it came true. Above all, I'm grateful to be walking away from the game healthy, happy and proud of everything I've experienced. It's been a journey I'll never forget."

What's your favourite Mustapha Carayol moment? Let us know in the comments.

Carayol isn't stepping away from football completely, though. To end his message, the 38-year-old stated that he'll be moving into football agency, "helping players navigate their careers and prepare for life beyond the game."

With Carayol playing for 19 different sides throughout his 19-year career, there were plenty of people who the 38-year-old connected with and played alongside. Those came to the comments section of his Instagram post announcing his retirement to credit him.

The official Middlesbrough account commented on both Instagram and X, "Congrats Muzzy 👏." Carayol's 124 Championship appearances started at the Riverside, after Boro signed him from Bristol Rovers after he recorded 13 goal contributions for the then-League Two side in 2011/12.

Of his former teammates, compatriot and current Portsmouth midfielder Ebou Adams commented, "Legend!!! Unreal career and achievements ❤️🔥👏." Lincoln City captain Tendayi Darikwa, who spent time with him at Nottingham Forest, wrote, "Congrats bro ❤️."

It wasn't just those who Carayol shared a dressing room with who praised his career, though. Former Crystal Palace and Everton winger Yannick Bolaise also spoke highly of the 38-year-old in his comments.

"Never played with you together felt like I did though congratulations my bro love every time 🙌❤️," he said.

Carayol was seemingly building himself as a solid goalscoring Championship winger during his time at Middlesbrough. There may have been some question marks surrounding his ability to step up from League Two at Bristol Rovers, but he did so successfully.

The wideman netted three and assisted two in just 18 league appearances in his first year on Teesside, and in his second season, scored eight and assisted three in just over 2,000 minutes of action — averaging a goal involvement every other game.

Unfortunately, an ACL injury suffered in March 2014 against Bournemouth ruled him out for a long period of time, and would actually turn out to be his final appearance for Middlesbrough.

Football League World takes an in-depth look at the TEN most frustrating EFL Championship players right now

By the time he was fit again, Boro were challenging for promotion under Aitor Karanka, and he spent his final years at the club out on loan with Brighton, Huddersfield and Leeds. He wasn't able to showcase his goalscoring knack pre-injury in those spells.

If Carayol hadn't gone down with that ACL injury, perhaps he could have remained a key part of a Middlesbrough side that was set for some good years under the Spaniard, and he could have played Premier League football in his career, too.

Either way, the winger retires with plenty of accolades both domestically and internationally, and his announcement has left a lot of fans looking back on his time with their club.

#2233. Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham

Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they fell to a pre-season friendly loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, moments after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Moments later Smith was on the scoresheet at the other end and it looked all too easy as he was left with a tap-in after O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

Sam Smith with the winning moment 🤌🔴⚪️#WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/YzTvnzIpz6

Twenty-one of the 22 players were replaced at half-time, with only Wrexham’s Aaron James staying on, and Carrick sent out a side entirely composed of academy products, facing a decent test against a Wrexham side now including the likes of Conor Coady and Kieffer Moore.

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Instead, Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’ cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target, but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Dan Gore hit the deck in the single minute of stoppage time, but his optimistic penalty appeal was waved away.

We knew it wouldn’t be perfect - that’s only natural for the first pre-season game - and the main thing is that everybody came through it in good shape. No injuries so we can move onto the next step next week.

[Andrey Santos] and Mason [Mount] did some really good things and connected really well. There’s loads of little positives to take. The sharpness at the top end will come as we move through pre-season.

I was really pleased with the second half team. They controlled the game really well against a team who aren’t easy to play against. The boys took responsibility and their quality; they can really be proud of themselves.

Man Utd appeal unsuccessfully for a penalty when Dan Gore goes over in the area. Seconds later, the referee blows the final whistle. Wrexham, who were under pressure for much of the second half, have held on to beat Manchester United in a muted pre-season friendly in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal in the 39th minute, having headed against his own crossbar three minutes earlier. There were 21 changes at half-time, 11 for Man Utd and 10 for Wrexham.

Andrey Santos, part of an experienced first-half XI, had a decent debut after signing from Chelsea in the week. Wheatley finds the underlapping Amass, whose pullback is cleared a little desperately by Wrexham. Amass, still only 19, looks really promising at left-back.

Ward makes another comfortable save, this time when Shea Lacey tries his luck from 22 yards.

Man Utd’s best move of the second half. Dan Gore runs onto a return pass from Shea Lacey and sweeps a low ball into the six-yard box that is held at the second attempt by Danny Ward.

Wrexham substitution Alex Moore replaces Aaron James, who was the only starter on either side to play part of the second half.

Kamason is booked for a late tackle on Dobson. That looked a bit harsh, certainly in a friendly.

Wrexham - in a back five, heaven forfend - are defending well and keeping the opposition at arm’s length. Unlike Argentina, Man Utd haven’t really tried any crosses yet.

No attempts at goal in the second half, on or off target, from either team. But the young Man Utd side have played some purposeful stuff and have had around 66% possession.

No chances to report but the young Man Utd side have started well, dominating possession and playing with greater urgency than their elders.

Man Utd (4-2-3-1) Vitek; Kamason, Devaney, Armer, Amass; Collyer, T Fletcher; Lacey, Gore, Williams; Wheatley.

39 min: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1 (Smith) Sam Smith gives Wrexham the lead. It came from a well-worked throw-in on the left. Thomason played a one-two before slipping a crisp pass into O’Brien in the area. His precise low cross, through the legs of Maguire, gave Smith a tap-in from three yards.

We’ve been back in training 10 days and we’re taking it step by step. It’s great to be back at it again.

Youri Tielemans is targeting more silverware after completing his £35m move to Manchester United.

Tielemans has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford after United triggered his release clause at Aston Villa.

The Belgium international played a key role in helping Villa lift the Europa League last season, but pushed for the move to United after turning down the offer of a new contract in the West Midlands.

“The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies,” he said.

“Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football. I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.”

I’m not sure when Man Utd last played Wrexham in a friendly, but the most recent competitive meeting between the sides was in January 1995. It was three days after Eric Cantona tried to kick xenophobia out of football at Selhurst Park, so United’s 5-2 win was somewhat overshadowed.

Andrey Santos starts in what is a pretty strong United XI.

Lining up for our first fixture of pre-season! 🇫🇮Watch LIVE on MUTV ⤵️

Our first-half XI in Helsinki 🇫🇮🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/WrXbc2B7JQ

The World Cup final? Pah! The 2026-27 Premier League season is just over a month away, and Manchester United’s pre-season begins this afternoon with a friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki.

Man Utd have started many seasons with a whimper since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, but there’s plenty of summer optimism around Old Trafford. Michael Carrick overachieved so spectacularly as caretaker manager that a full-time appointment became inevitable. Now all he has to do is maintain that league form across a full season while also juggling the Champions League.

United have filled part of their midfield void by signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. Tielemans is having a post-World Cup break but Santos is part of a United squad that also includes Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro.

“Everything about Manchester United is special,” said Santos after signing for the club earlier in the week. “It is an incredible feeling to join a club that some of my biggest idols have represented. As a midfielder, I am really excited to have the opportunity to learn from Michael Carrick. He is the perfect coach to help me take the next step in my career and push to achieve my dreams.”

Wrexham have ambitions to play United in a competitive fixture sooner rather than later. They missed out on the Championship playoffs but will go again with a very similar squad.

“This is a great test for us, it really is,” said their manager Phil Parkinson. “As always, when we were in the other divisions we looked to these games as a test and this will be absolutely no different.

“The out-of-possession stuff becomes really important against the better quality teams. But as we’ve always done, we’re not just going to these games to stop the opposition.”

#2232. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2231. How Dave Challinor’s strongest Sheffield Wednesday XI will look as new boss gets to work

Sheffield Wednesday confirmed Dave Challinor’s appointment as first-team manager over the weekend, and after watching the 1-1 draw with Blackpool from the stands, he starts his work now.

The former Stockport County boss is tasked with leading SWFC back to the Championship as they rebuild after relegation and administration. He has a strong squad at his disposal, and the pressure is on to succeed where the departed Henrik Pedersen failed.

One of the first challenges Challinor faces is to identify his strongest and favoured starting XI. His squad is brimming with talent and boasts depth in all areas, so there is strong competition for a place in the plans of the new manager.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Weaver; Valery, Mitchell, Slattery, M. Lowe; Barry, Keillor-Dunn; Burstow

The Owls’ summer rebuild means they have good squad depth across the board, so Challinor will be able to tinker with his setup as he works out the best XI. However, there will be a familiar feel to the setup, as the 51-year-old’s preferred formation has been 3-4-2-1 over the course of his career.

This setup was Pedersen’s go-to last season, although he occasionally switched to a 3-1-4-2 or 3-5-2 at times. Danny Rohl also used a 3-4-2-1 during his tenure, but like Pedersen, he switched to a 4-2-3-1 – which Challinor has deployed too – later in his reign.

As for the personnel, Joe Lumley will be backed to reclaim his starting spot from Ashley Maynard-Brewer when fit.

The centre-back positions will be a point of contention, with all of Di’Shon Bernard, Liam Cooper, Ernie Weaver, Ricardo Santos, Sil Swinkels, Gabriel Otegbayo and the versatile Max Lowe to pick from. All of those players could feasibly start, but Bernard has been a Championship standout at his best, Cooper provides leadership, experience and a left-footed presence for balance, and Weaver has the highest ceiling of the lot.

Yan Valery seems a shoo-in for Challinor’s right wing-back spot, and Lowe should be favoured on the left.

In the middle, Callum Slattery could emerge as Billy Mitchell’s regular partner with Barry Bannan enduring a tricky start to the campaign. This is another area where competition is strong, with all of Bannan, Jaden Heskey and Jarvis Thornton up for consideration while Tyler Onyango recovers from his ACL injury.

In the two roles behind the striker, Davis Keillor-Dunn is emerging as an influential player, and Louie Barry will be backed to land a key role when fit given his past success under Challinor. Slattery could also play in one of these advanced roles.

Up top, Mason Burstow could get the nod over top scorer Jamal Lowe. Again, there is strong depth here with Harry Gray, Ali Al-Hamadi, Will Grainger and Keillor-Dunn all capable of playing at striker.

The 3-4-2-1 has been Challinor’s go-to, but a 3-5-2 at Sheffield Wednesday could see Barry start as a striker with a midfield three of Mitchell, Slattery and Heskey or Bannan.

A 4-2-3-1 would facilitate a similar midfield, while a centre-back drops out. The depth in the SWFC squad means Challinor is spoiled for choice as he works out his best lineup.

Challinor has plenty of experience now, but this is a new task for him. With the greatest respect to his previous jobs, Sheffield Wednesday are a different beast in terms of club stature and expectation.

At Stockport County and AFC Fylde, he built them into teams that were truly his, and they grew over time. At Hillsborough, he faces the task of getting the most out of a group with big names and personalities. It will be a test of his abilities as both a coach and man manager.

Challinor’s record is excellent, but this is the biggest challenge he has faced in his managerial career to date.

#2230. Jerry Yates drops claim about Sheffield Wednesday's atmosphere

Jerry Yates has paid Sheffield Wednesday and their fans a big compliment following Blackpool’s 1-1 draw at Hillsborough on Sunday.

Davis Keillor-Dunn gave the hosts the lead after 25 minutes, but the Owls were soon down to 10 men after Sil Swinkels was given his marching orders.

Yates then found the back of the net in the closing stages to secure a point for the Tangerines in what was Matt Hamshaw’s final game in charge of the club in this interim stint.

Dave Challinor has been confirmed as the new Sheffield Wednesday boss, and has taken the reins on Monday, with the aim of guiding the team to a promotion push this season.

Meanwhile, Blackpool earned just their 12th point from 12 league games so far this campaign, with the club hoping to avoid a relegation battle.

This was Yates’ third goal of the term, having also found the back of the net in a 4-0 win against Peterborough United and in a 4-2 loss to Plymouth Argyle.

Yates has claimed that playing against Sheffield Wednesday at Hillsborough is like playing against an extra man anyway, such is the impact of the home crowd.

He believes the Owls are a massive side, having previously spent time on loan at the Yorkshire outfit last season, meaning he knows just how much of an impact the supporters can have.

Former Sheffield Wednesday starlet Josh Windass has reacted to the Owls' impending appointment of Clint Hill alongside Dave Challinor

“I think it’s tough to play against 10 men, as we all know,” said Yates, via Blackpool on X.

“Obviously a massive side, crowd gets behind them.

“You sometimes feel like they’ve got an extra man anyway with the crowd and stuff like that.”

Yates moved to Sheffield Wednesday on loan from Luton Town during the January transfer window last season.

He arrived shortly before the Owls’ relegation to League One was confirmed, with the club struggling for results amid their dire financial situation.

The striker still managed to contribute four goals from 18 appearances in the Championship before returning to the Hatters in the summer.

Sheffield Wednesday fans have responded positively to Yates’ comments, suggesting that he loves the club after just a short stint on loan there.

The 29-year-old is fondly remembered by supporters, despite only spending half a season at Hillsborough.

Fans also noticed how often he said the word massive, which they have taken as a big compliment.

Some supporters have even suggested that the Owls should have sought a deal to bring Yates back to Hillsborough for this season.

Next up for Sheffield Wednesday is a trip to face Oldham Athletic on 8 November in a 5.15pm kick-off.

Sheffield Wednesday have obviously left a mark on Yates after just half-a-season as part of the first team squad.

The crowd will be pleased to hear they have this kind of impact on the team, and that kind of advantage is something Challinor will now be hoping to utilise.

The Owls have the biggest stadium in League One, and are a club that should be targeting a return to the Championship as quickly as possible.

And this kind of respect that they receive from opposition is a sign of where they stand in the pecking order in the division this year.

#2229. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Harry Maguire-5.5            Was decent in the first half but wasn’t much of an answer to Tottenham going forward in the second half

Lisandro Martinez-5      Took his eyes off the ball, resulting in conceding a late goal off Solanke.

Luke Shaw-6      Went up high on the pitch and remained a threat with his overlapping threat. Was involved in the scuffle that got Bentancur a red card for headbutting.

Kobbie Mainoo-6.5        Brilliant defensive tackle to deny Tottenham in the 68th minute. Remained composed in tight spaces against a physical Tottenham midfield.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

#2228. Kilmarnock 2-2 St Johnstone: Ten-man visitors battle back for well-earned point

St Johnstone battled to a terrific 2-2 draw with 10 men as Kilmarnock’s woes continued.

Simo Valakari’s side were at a disadvantage from the 13th minute following the dismissal of goalkeeper Toby Steward for handling outside of his area.

Yet despite going behind immediately after the red card to Cathal McCarthy’s first goal, Saints were never out of the game.

They levelled through Danny Schmidt after 40 minutes, only for Djenairo Daniels to restore the home lead before half-time.

However, a breakaway goal from Joel Cotterill after 65 minutes was enough to claim an unlikely point.

Killie passed up a glut of chances for victory, with substitute keeper Ross Sinclair’s saves and desperate, durable defending from the visitors leaving Killie boss Neil McCann visibly frustrated.

The point was enough to lift them off the bottom of the William Hill Premiership table, but this was a golden chance to do so much more and conceding 28 goals in 12 games makes sorry reading.

The tone of the contest was transformed by Steward’s folly after just 10 minutes when the on-loan Portsmouth man gathered a long ball outside his penalty box.

Joe Hugill was the Kilmarnock player on the premises but Steward appeared to have time to take a step back before collecting.

However, VAR signalled referee Matthew MacDermid to check for denial of a goalscoring opportunity and Steward knew his fate.

Back-up keeper Sinclair, on for Taylor Steven, then touched the ball for the first time when picking it out of his net.

From the spot of the foul, Killie worked a set-piece for Greg Kiltie to deliver an inswinger and McCarthy met it six-yards out with a headed finish to score the first goal of his loan spell from Hull City.

Daniels thought he had doubled the lead after 31 minutes from a tight angle before an offside flag foiled him.

Kilmarnock’s defensive problems first came back to bite them, even with the personnel advantage, five minutes before half-time.

Josh Fowler was denied by an excellent fingertip stop by German keeper Nico Mantl but, from the corner, Enes Alic’s delivery was headed into the far corner by an unmarked Schmidt.

Kilmarnock did not dwell on their misfortune and hit straight back. Hugill scampered up the left flank and his cutback was buried by a brilliant backheel flick from Daniels.

Aaron Tshibola spurned the best chance to bury Saints after 63 minutes. Hugill’s brilliant backheel left the DR Congo international staring down Sinclair but he shot weakly and straight at the keeper.

Saints then stunned Killie in the 65th minute to level once more.

The counter-attack came from a Kilmarnock corner breaking down and Alic picked out Cotterill with a great pass. The Welshman sped beyond two defenders to lash in a low finish for 2-2.

Nicky Clescenco came within inches of putting Killie back in front after Tyreece John-Jules nicked the ball from Diabate.

Sinclair then batted away from George Stanger and made a superb reaction stop to deny John-Jules from close range as Kilmarnock failed to find the breakthrough.

#2227. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2226. Birmingham City to change club badge? Social media 'confirmation' clears up situation

Birmingham City are a club looking to move in one clear direction both on and off the pitch, and the ambition at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park has certainly been matched by performances in the here and now.

The 2026/27 Championship season is the fourth term of Knighthead Capital Management's ownership tenure in the Second City, as well as Blues' third with Chris Davies as manager.

Davies has endured mixed fortunes since the beginning of his first full-time position, seeing a record-breaking campaign in League One followed up by a 10th-placed finish last season, albeit it was still the highest Birmingham had finished since the 2015/16 campaign.

After an intriguing summer which saw seven new players recruited and five depart, as well as the exit of Craig Gardner as director of football, the club has since made further changes.

Following a period of strong speculation, it was recently confirmed that former Manchester United, Everton and Atlanta higher-up, John Murtough, had filled the void left by Gardner's departure.

Since then, Davies' side have lost at Cardiff City and defeated Lincoln City, seeing them sit sixth in the Championship ahead of Tuesday's clash with Millwall, which coincides with the release of a new marketing campaign.

Birmingham's ownership group have explored many ways to improve transparency between themselves and supporters who were previously disillusioned.

Such feats have included 'Open House' events in which several elements of the club's day-to-day progress have been discussed and plans have been unveiled, such as the upcoming 62,000-seater Powerhouse Stadium.

Although a name of the upcoming campaign remains unrevealed, Blues' social media pages have released a selection of teaser videos highlighting its release on Tuesday.

"We have built a campaign that reflects the bold ambition we have set and can’t wait to share it with you," read a sentence on the club's website on October 28th.

With many fans speculating what the campaign could centre around, one supporter commented: "Don’t you dare touch the badge. This is our club, a football club."

They were then left assured that Blues' 'globe and ball' badge, which was designed in 1972, would remain untouched, as the club responded: "Admin can confirm no changes to the badge."

Football ownership has become a strong topic in recent years, with those responsible for making the key decisions often looking to bring elements of their own culture to the club whilst embracing local traditions.

Knighthead have done their utmost to immerse themselves in the habits of Blues fans, but the aforementioned supporter's concern could well have stemmed from Vincent Tan's high-profile decision to change Cardiff City's identity in 2012.

Indeed, the Bluebirds changed their historic crest and colours to red due to Tan's home country of Malaysia believing it brings luck, which, to an extent, worked as Cardiff were promoted as champions at the end of said season.

However, it also led to major unrest in South Wales and the decision was eventually reversed in January 2015 with the club back in the Championship.

Which Championship owners currently cause the most and least friction? FLW takes a look...

Whilst Birmingham's badge is unaffected, the club have since released a sit-down interview with chief marketing officer, Liam McManus, with a small section of the discussion posted on X, showcasing that the campaign's main focus is on what could happen at the Powerhouse.

"Doing it now means that we keep the sense of momentum. We keep the sense of progress. This club is moving fast and we want to keep that sense of momentum up," said McManus.

Blues fans, what do you expect from the upcoming marketing campaign? Comment below!

The club's future home is said to not just be about the evolution of Birmingham City as a brand, but also that of the Bordesley Green area, with several commercial and retail hubs set to be opened, in turn creating a multitude of career opportunities for those in Birmingham and the wider West Midlands.

#2225. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2224. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”
